<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par72 />since the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of {{GHGheb|text=קוּטֹ}} appears as {{GHGheb|text=אָקוּט}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=95|verse=10}}. On the other hand {{GHGheb|text=יְקשׁוּן}} (as if from {{GHGheb|text=קוֹשׁ}}, on the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=יָבוֹא}}, &c.) occurs as {{GHGterm|imperfect}} of {{GHGheb|text=יָקשׁ}} ({{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}). The {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יָדוֹן}}, with ''ô'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=3}}, probably in the sense of ''to rule'', has no corresponding {{GHGterm|perfect}}, and is perhaps intentionally differentiated from the common verb {{GHGheb|text=יָדִין|translate=to judge}} (from {{GHGheb|text=דִּין}}, {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}}). Or can {{GHGheb|text=יָדוֹן}} be a {{GHGterm|jussive}} after {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} (cf. {{GHGpar|109|d}})? Similarly {{GHGheb|text=לֹא תָחוֹס עֵינִי (עֵֽינְךָ)}} might be taken as a case of a jussive after {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}}, with irregular ''scriptio plena'' (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=30}}), in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=19|verse=13.21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=25|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=4.9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=10|hidebook=1}}. But perhaps in all these cases {{GHGheb|text=לֹא תָחוּס}} was originally intended, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=21|verse=7}}, while cases like {{GHGheb|text=יָחֹס}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=13}} are to be explained as in {{GHGpar|109|k}}.—The {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} always has ''ô'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קוֹם יָק֫וּמוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=29}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|s}}
3. In the {{GHGterm|imperative}} with afformatives ({{GHGheb|text=ק֫וּמִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=ק֫וּמוּ}}) the tone is on the stem syllable (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=עוּרִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=12}} intentionally varied from {{GHGheb|text=ע֫וּרִי}}; also {{GHGheb|text=עוּרִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=13|verse=7}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=9}} beside {{GHGheb|text=ע֫וּרִי כִּ֣ימֵי}}; {{GHGheb|text=גִּילִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=צוּרִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּבִ֫י}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=116|verse=7}}, likewise for rhythmical reasons). So also the lengthened form, as {{GHGheb|text=שׁ֫וּבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=8}}, and {{GHGheb|text=ע֫וּרָה}} verse 7. But if an {{GHGheb|text=א}} follows in close connexion, the lengthened {{GHGterm|imperative}} usually has the form {{GHGheb|text=קוּמָ֫ה}}, &c.,<ref>Cf. Delitzsch’s commentary on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=8}}.</ref> in order to avoid a hiatus, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=82|verse=8}}; hence also before {{GHGheb|text=יְהֹוָה}}, ''Q<sup>e</sup>rê perpetuum'' {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי}} ({{GHGpar|17|c}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=7|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=קוּמָ֫ה}} (cf., however, in the same verse {{GHGheb|text=ע֫וּרָה}} and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=5}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֻׁ֫בָה}} before {{GHGheb|text=א}}), and so even before {{GHGheb|text=ר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=43|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, &c. ({{GHGheb|text=רִיבָ֫ה}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|t}}
4. In the {{GHGterm|jussive}}, besides the form {{GHGheb|text=יָקֹם}} (see above, f), {{GHGheb|text=יָקוֹם}} also occurs (as subjunctive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָסוֹג}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=80|verse=19}} may also, with Delitzsch, be regarded as a voluntative), incorrectly written {{GHGterm|plene}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יָקֻ֫ם}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=31}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=4.16}}), which, however, is only orthographically different from {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=6}}). In the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}} ({{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קָם}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קֹם}}, see above, f) if there be a guttural or {{GHGheb|text=ר}} in the last syllable, ''ă'' often takes the place of ''ŏ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫נַח|translate=and he rested}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫נַע|translate=and it was moved}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫סַר|translate=and he turned aside}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=1}} (distinguished only by the sense from {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫סַר|translate=and he removed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=13}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫צַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=5|hidebook=1}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫גָר}} from both {{GHGheb|text=גּוּר|translate=to sojourn}}, and {{GHGheb|text=גּוּר|translate=to fear}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫עַף}} (to be distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫עָף|translate=and he flew}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=6}}) ''and he was weary'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=28.31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=15}}, but probably in all these cases {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּעַף}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּיעַף}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָעֵף}} is intended. For {{GHGheb|text=ותלוש}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=8}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, the Q<sup>e</sup>rê rightly requires {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּ֫לָשׁ}}. On the other hand, in an open syllable always {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּק֫וּמוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּס֫וּרוּ}}, &c. On {{GHGheb|text=(וָאָֽקֻם) וָאָֽקוּם}}, see {{GHGpar|49|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|u}}
Examples of the full plural ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} with the tone (see above, l) are {{GHGheb|text=תְּמֻת֫וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=3.4}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְנוּס֫וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְרוּצ֫וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=2|verse=4.7.9}}.

{{center|II. ''On Niphʿal''. }}

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|v}}
5. The form of the 1st ''sing. perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=נְקוּמ֫וֹתִי}}, which frequently occurs ({{GHGheb|text=נְסוּגֹ֫תִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְפוּגֹ֫תִי}}, cf. also the ''ptcp. plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=נְכוּכִים}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=3}}), serves as a model for the 2nd ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=נְקוּמ֫וֹתָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְקוּמוֹת}}, and the 1st ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=נְקוּמ֫וֹנוּ}} given in the paradigm, although no instances of these forms are found; but of the 2nd ''plur.'' the<section end=par72 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
